description: Minimum cost of a path using exactly D edges in an implicit complete Monge DAG.

source.title: d-Edge Shortest-Path Problem for a Monge Graph
source.algorithm_attribution: exact-edge DP layers with monotone minima over a triangular Monge transition matrix

input.vertex_ids: 0 through N; implicit directed edge i->j exists exactly when i<j
input.edge_weight_order: Upper-triangle row-major order by increasing source, then increasing destination.
input.monge_promise: For every fully valid adjacent quadrangle with i+1<j, c(i,j)+c(i+1,j+1) <= c(i,j+1)+c(i+1,j); ports validate this local form.

output.meaning: Minimum sum of edge weights on a path from vertex 0 to vertex N that uses exactly D edges.

workspace.meaning: Triangular edge-cost matrix, two exact-edge DP rows, monotone-minima recursion stack, and predecessor minima.

contract.path_domain: The graph is the complete forward DAG over vertices 0..N; every edge increases the vertex ID.
contract.objective: Find the cheapest 0-to-N path containing exactly D edges.
contract.optimization: For each edge-count layer, argmin predecessors are nondecreasing by the Monge property; monotone divide-and-conquer row minima compute the layer without enumerating all transitions.
contract.distinction: This is an implicit complete Monge-DAG exact-edge path DP, not explicit-graph shortest paths or a min-plus matrix-power walk query.

complexity.primary_time: O(D*N*log(N)) monotone divide-and-conquer minima after O(N^2) input validation
